About 10 minutes in the gym

Returnto run3 tests

Coming back to running after knee pain? These are three gym tests I use to see where a runner's at. Type your numbers in as you go and the page does the maths.

Mitch Scott, Physiotherapist and Exercise Physiologist. MEO Rehab & Performance, Pinnacle Fitness Albion, Brisbane.

kg

Every test below is worked out against it.

Before you start

  • Warm up properly first. Don't test cold.
  • If you're currently doing a rehab program, check with your healthcare provider before you do any of these tests.
  • This is education only. It isn't medical advice or training advice.

If any of these hurt, that'd be a yellow flag already.

Don't push through it to get a number. Stop that test and get it looked at.

01

Leg extension

One leg at a time. Find the heaviest weight you can lift for 5 clean reps, then do the other leg.

Demo video

Left, 5-rep max
kg
Right, 5-rep max
kg

Each side as a % of your bodyweight. What I look for: 80% or more.

Gap between sides (what I look for: under 10%)–
02

Hamstring bridge hold

Single leg. Forefoot on a foam roller, heel high, hips up. Hold as long as you can, then swap legs.

Demo video

Left, hold time
sec
Right, hold time
sec

What I look for: at least 30 seconds each side.

Gap between sides–
03

Smith machine single-leg calf raise

One leg at a time. Find the heaviest load you can do for 5 full reps. Type in the plates you added. The 10 kg bar gets added for you.

Demo video

Left, plates added
kg
Right, plates added
kg

Includes the 10 kg bar. If your gym's Smith bar is different, change it here: kg

Total load (plates plus bar) as a % of your bodyweight. What I look for: 50% or more to start. The long-term goal is 100%. You might never hit it, but I want you to try.

Your numbers stay on this page. Nothing is saved or sent anywhere, so copy them if you want to keep them.

One honest limit.

These numbers show where you're at. On their own, they don't tell you whether you're ready to run. That depends on the rest of the picture: how the knee responds the next morning, how much you were running before, and what you're building back to.
